P15-001.grounds: Three sub-claims upheld, one refined. (a) UPHELD (engagement class): the close is argued from a shift to a communal first-person-plural voice at the next verse, but no pointed form is quoted at oshb:Isa.52.15 or oshb:Isa.53.1 anywhere in the row -- the row's single Hebrew splice is its onset -- and neither verse appears under an oshb: ref. A boundary-relevant Hebrew form claim owes a pointed splice and a tier. In the bytes the shift is real -- לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte; unique at every tier) carries the first-person-plural suffix -- so the conclusion is byte-supportable; the defect is that it is carried entirely by the English rendering as written. (b) UPHELD and the strongest item: the row's own discriminator cuts INSIDE the span and is never named. oshb:Isa.52.13 speaks of the figure in the third person (עַבְדִּ֑י, with a third-person verb); oshb:Isa.52.14 addresses him in the second person masculine singular, עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ (byte; byte-unique to that verse), which the second witness renders as direct address; oshb:Isa.52.15 returns to the third person, עָלָ֛יו (byte). The rationale calls web:Isa.52.14-Isa.52.15 one continuous astonished-nations description. The internal shift is sharper than the one used to argue the close -- a second-person direct address against a third-to-first-plural voice change -- and applying the test at one seam while passing over it twice inside the span is the defect. (c) REFINED on both hooks: the arm hook is real but weaker and differently placed than OL says. וּזְר֥וֹעַ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte) against זְר֣וֹעַ קָדְשׁ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.52.10, byte): collation of the oshb:Isa.52.10 token against oshb:Isa.53.1 reaches accent_stripped, the reverse returns none. OL's 'exactly 4 verses' is not reproducible under any consistent object -- word-bound skeleton gives 3 (oshb:Isa.51.9, oshb:Isa.52.10, oshb:Isa.63.12), prefix-tolerant word-bound gives 6 (adding oshb:Isa.44.12, oshb:Isa.53.1, oshb:Isa.62.8), and the bare substring gives 8 while blending the sowing root at oshb:Isa.61.11 -- and this is the SAME erratum OL carries in its P14-021 item. The hook also runs from a verse OUTSIDE this span to a verse one past its close, so it argues a motif chain across three rows, not against this row's own seam. The hearing hook is weaker still: שָׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.52.15, byte) and לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ collate to none against each other and share only a three-letter root as a consonantal substring, a substring that reaches 30 verses book-wide. Under the word-binding discipline that is a root-level echo, not a byte-true device, and it does not carry the continuity argument OL rests on it. Disclosure of both is worth a device note; neither contests the cut at the strength claimed. (d) UPHELD: the onset הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י (oshb:Isa.52.13, byte) is called a divine first-person oracle-opening formula in the rationale while the rejected alternative concedes that no explicit frame formula marks a fresh oracle boundary here -- the row contradicts itself. The bytes support the concession, not the label: the presentative particle is verse-initial at 21 verses book-wide and present at 46, and it belongs to NONE of this book's frame-spine objects (not the messenger formula, not the woe-cry, not an oracle header, not the divine-speech signature); the verb is third-person; only the suffix on the servant noun is first-person. And the servant noun is then filed under a divine-title signal class, which misassigns it -- this book's divine-title objects are the tetragrammaton, adonai, the of-hosts title, the Holy-One-of-Israel title and the short form; עַבְדִּ֑י is the servant designation with a first-person suffix, a servant-census object (23 verses), and the row already carries two correct servant keys. Two further SHAPES sit inside object (i)'s family but are not the adjacent formula: אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (MT 54:8) and אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (MT 54:10) each interpose a participial epithet. The discriminating object is the four-token contour: רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה (MT 54:1) and עֲנִיָּ֥ה סֹעֲרָ֖ה לֹ֣א נֻחָ֑מָה (MT 54:11) carry an IDENTICAL accent sequence — merkha, tipcha, munach, etnachta — over the same vocative-plus-negative-plus-qatal shape, and MT 54:1 is the row's own front-seam warrant. But OL OVERSTATES its consequence: MT 54:11 addresses the SAME feminine addressee, so the row's 'no fresh addressee or scene shift' survives literally; the defect is non-disclosure of a live rival cut, not a false universal. So symmetry fails on the paseq layer alone. NEW FINDING neither primary made: the seam is not warrantless — what DOES change at MT 55:6 is the addressee NUMBER, back to masculine plural after the masculine singular of MT 55:5, which is a byte-real tier-1 warrant the row never states. One imprecision in OL's own citation: MT 55:3's attested token is the waw-prefixed form, not the bare imperative it names (the bare form is a substring of it). P15-006.challenge_claim: The row walls its rear seam off from texture argument while a byte-identical run straddles that very seam undisclosed, and its front-seam warrant repeats the non-discriminating imperative claim used at the web:Isa.55.5|web:Isa.55.6 seam.
P15-006.grounds: Credit verified: both splices reach byte tier at oshb:Isa.55.6 and oshb:Isa.55.8; נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה stands verse-final at MT 55:8 and that pointed run is byte tier in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, MT 55:8 and MT 59:20; 6 verses accent-stripped); the ketiv/qere at MT 55:13 is described exactly right, the unpointed ketiv running immediately into the conjunction-prefixed pointed qere as the doubled pair תחת וְתַ֥חַת; and the parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 55:13 in-span, MT 55:5 at the front seam) with 0 paseq segs across MT 55:6-55:13. The cross-seam finding is UPHELD and its digits are exact: לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת closes MT 55:13, this row's final verse, and לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת closes MT 56:5, three verses past the seam, BYTE-IDENTICAL — that pointed run stands at byte tier in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses) and its consonantal skeleton in exactly 3 (sweep: 3 verses, MT 48:19, 55:13, 56:5), so the pairing across the seam is not incidental. Declaring the seam 'non-negotiable independent of any internal-texture argument' is precisely the exemption the cross-seam disclosure rule forbids: a byte-true device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against it unless disclosed. REFINED in the row's favour on one point: this seam is the ratified parent-frame boundary at web:Isa.55.13|web:Isa.56.1, and rows never straddle a frame seam, so the device provably CANNOT move it — the cure is disclosure only, never a respan, and the row is right that the seam itself is not at stake. The front-seam item is UPHELD as the mirror of the defect adjudicated at the web:Isa.55.5|web:Isa.55.6 seam: one seam argued from both sides is a seam pair whose cure is ONE edit. NEW FINDING neither primary made: this row breaches the register purge in two fields — boundary_rationale has the row running to 'this part's own rear frame boundary' and device_notes calls the seam 'the part-boundary frame seam'. Both name the writer's own batch structure rather than the seam's place in Isaiah's text, which is barred in EVERY field. The seam is genuinely the ratified frame boundary, so only the wording is defective — and the same class was challenged on neighbouring rows, so the cure is a sweep across the part, not a spot fix.
P15-006.remedy: Author work order. (a) device_notes: REPLACE the exemption sentence with a cross-seam disclosure — the closing run is byte-identical at oshb:Isa.55.13 and oshb:Isa.56.5 (byte tier, sweep: 2 verses; skeleton 3 verses including MT 48:19) — and state that the seam is a preserved larger-unit boundary the device cannot move. TEST (the check that killed the original): collate the spliced run to byte tier at both refs and re-run both sweeps to 2 and 3 verses. (b) boundary_rationale: replace 'a further imperative distinguishable from the invitation cry' with the addressee-number fact — the addressee returns to masculine plural at MT 55:6 while the imperative form-class is unchanged — as ONE edit shared with the row ending at web:Isa.55.5, in a distinct formulation. TEST: as ordered there. (c) boundary_rationale AND device_notes: purge the part/batch wording — name the seam by its place in Isaiah's own text (the frame boundary at web:Isa.55.13|web:Isa.56.1), never by the writer's assigned range. TEST: no field may contain a phrase naming a part, batch, assigned range or row order; run the purge over the whole part, not this row alone.
